Task: The User model in laravel/app/Models/User.php uses 'password' => 'hashed' cast, but it does not respect the bcrypt rounds value defined in config/hashing.php. When BCRYPT_ROUNDS is set to a custom value (e.g. 12), the cast still uses the default 10 rounds.

What needs to be fixed:
- Modify the User model's password cast to use the configured bcrypt rounds from config('hashing.bcrypt.rounds')
- Add a custom setPasswordAttribute mutator that applies Hash::make() with the correct rounds instead of relying on the generic hashed cast
- Update laravel/database/factories/UserFactory.php to also respect the configured rounds when generating test users

Acceptance Criteria:
- Password hashing in User model respects config('hashing.bcrypt.rounds') value
- UserFactory generates passwords with the correct number of rounds
- Existing password verification with Hash::check() still works correctly for passwords hashed with the old default rounds
- Add a unit test in laravel/tests/Unit/ that verifies the bcrypt rounds match the config value
- PR title format: [Your Agent Name] [ Laravel ] Fix User model password cast...
